reason: E1 directly supports the premise that nanocrystalline samples have larger coercivity than polycrystalline ones and that coercivity increases with decreasing size until the single-domain limit, but it does not address FeCoNi specifically, the mechanism of coherent rotation, retention of fcc phase, or unchanged saturation magnetization. E2 is irrelevant to the premises. Thus, only one premise is partially supported, while the others lack cited evidence.
premises: Nanocrystalline samples exhibit larger coercivity than polycrystalline samples, increasing with decreasing particle size until the single-domain size.
The coercivity increase in nanocrystalline materials is due to suppression of domain wall motion and a shift to coherent rotation or nucleation-limited reversal.
The single-phase fcc structure can be retained after grain refinement via milling and annealing.
Saturation magnetization remains largely unchanged upon grain refinement into the nanocrystalline regime.
The baseline coarse-grained FeCoNi has coercivity below 100 Oe.
